newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end steady, profit-taking cuts gains.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end steady, profit-taking cuts gains.

text.p: Profit-taking by speculators wiped out early gains as Delhi share prices closed virtually unchanged in mixed trade on Monday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index ended 0.79 point higher at 780.66.
Earlier, the index had spurted to 787.17 in afternoon trade.
Brokers said buying was limited to select stocks.
Institutional investors snapped up shares of cigarette maker ITC and steel maker TISCO amid expectations the companies would announce strong 1996/97 (April-March) corporate results, brokers said.
"The market has shown some firmness but the gains were confined to some particular stocks which are likely to post better results," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
Market analysts said they expected the Calcutta-based firm to report sharply higher profits following robust growth in cigarette sales and improved margins.
ITC, which is scheduled to announce its 1996/97 results on Tuesday, closed 6.40 rupees higher at 447.40 on foreign buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 5.60 rupees to 310.80.
However, shares of auto manufacturer Bajaj Auto dropped 9.75 rupees to 870.00 on speculative selling.
